summary: The architecture has the right high-level split between scoring authority and application/UI duties, and it correctly treats hardware-in-the-loop as a later release gate. It does not yet meet reliability approval because protection, reset containment, event integrity, lifecycle proof, power margin, and production evidence are mostly assertions or placeholders rather than enforceable design artifacts.

findings.claim: External fencing interfaces are production-controllable and compatibility/protection-sensitive.
findings.correction: Do not treat the body-cord and piste interfaces as fabrication-ready. Replace ANALOG-FRONT-END-TBD and direct piste-to-MCU topology with a selected, reviewed analog/protection network covering excitation limits, ESD/surge, leakage, capacitance, line shorts, sweat/corrosion, and FIE resistance thresholds before layout release.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Schematic with selected parts, tolerance/temperature analysis, SPICE or equivalent front-end model, ESD/surge test plan, and socketed fixture results for foil/epee/sabre classifications.

findings.claim: The decision record is immutable and CRC-verified with full electrical history and replay integrity.
findings.correction: Make the implementation match the stated record model: include CRC or authenticated digest, rejection reasons, timing boundary metadata, firmware digest, boot identifiers, sequence ranges, RTC uncertainty, and ordered bounded sample validation. JSON parse plus type guards is not sufficient for production event integrity.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Protocol schema, CRC/authentication vectors, corrupted/truncated/reordered record tests, reboot replay corpus, and persistence fault-injection results.

findings.claim: Independent watchdogs, supervisors, and processor resets contain application faults while STM32 scoring remains authoritative.
findings.correction: Connect and verify watchdog and supervisor reset outputs to the appropriate processors and define fail-safe reset polarity/defaults across the isolation barrier. Current circuit evidence shows watchdog kick traces but not reset containment paths to the MCUs.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Netlist structural tests for reset paths, fault tree, injected ESP32 reset/corrupt-link tests, and STM32 continued-scoring evidence.

findings.claim: Separate scoring and application ground nets plus reinforced isolation are structurally protected.
findings.correction: Replace string-presence checks with netlist-level isolation checks proving no unintended SGND/GND bridge except through qualified isolated components. Add layout rules for creepage, clearance, slot geometry, shield/chassis handling, and isolated power return paths.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Automated net-class/ERC assertions, layout DRC constraints, isolation barrier review, creepage/clearance report, and shield bonding plan.

findings.claim: Manufacturer lifecycle, temperature, current, memory, isolation, and longevity claims are pinned to approved active components.
findings.correction: Do not accept lifecycle and qualification strings as self-certifying. Store primary manufacturer evidence per MPN with checked fields and dates, especially for lifecycle state, temperature grade, package/orderable variant, isolation certification, current limits, flash/PSRAM size, and the CY15B104Q-LHXIT preferred-through-2033 claim.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Machine-verifiable source snapshots or datasheet references for every listed MPN, plus a CI check that fails when required manufacturer fields are missing or stale.

findings.claim: Power and thermal margins are adequate for display, audio, networking, radio, and isolated scoring operation.
findings.correction: Treat the power tree as unproven. Define per-rail loads, converter efficiencies, eFuse branch sizing, HUB75 full-white current, audio peak load, isolated scoring-domain load, inductor/capacitor derating, and thermal limits before fabrication.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Worst-case power spreadsheet, selected inductor/capacitor data, branch protection schematic, thermal simulation, and later thermal-camera/thermocouple validation at worst-case operation.

findings.claim: Favero and Skewered compatibility is handled honestly.
findings.correction: Keep the current wording that no Favero wire compatibility is claimed unless a separately validated adapter exists. Any future compatibility statement must be protocol- and waveform-specific, not inferred from RS-485 isolation or display replay similarity.
findings.evidenceNeeded: Oscilloscope captures, electrical protocol conformance corpus, cable-length tests, mixed-device tests, and explicit non-copying display behavior review.
